schema.schemaVersion: Major shape of this file. 3 adds $schema, schema (this guide) and downloads; 2 added theme and marketing; 1 is the bare product record.
schema.$schema: The published JSON Schema for this file, so editors validate the kit as you type.
schema.schema: This block: every field of assets.json explained. Structure comes from lib/kit-doc.ts in the site repo — edit structure there, prose here.
schema.product.slug: URL-safe identifier; the site route is /work/<slug>/ and the press kit /press/<slug>/.
schema.product.name: Display name, spelled exactly as press.naming requires.
schema.product.category: "app" or "tool" — sorts the card into the two landing groups.
schema.product.headline.lead: First half of the headline duet.
schema.product.headline.lift: The italic-serif half of the headline. Required.
schema.product.tagline: One line under the headline on the card.
schema.product.summary: Longer one-liner for the product page hero and press kit.
schema.product.platform: Long-form platform string for the fact rows.
schema.product.licence.label: How the licence reads on the card.
schema.product.licence.kind: oss | free | paid — drives the label ink and JSON-LD offers.
schema.product.licence.price: Price line for the fact rows.
schema.product.licence.pricePoint: For kind "paid": the fragment that costs money, e.g. "$5 Pro".
schema.product.distribution: Where it is installed from, as a phrase.
schema.product.mono: Fallback monogram for an icon-less kit; null when an icon exists.
schema.links.repo: The repository's real https:// URL — the fetch script resolves it directly.
schema.links.store: Optional store listing (Mac App Store). Shown as a fact row and the hero fallback badge.
schema.press.short: One-paragraph boilerplate for the press kit.
schema.press.long: Full boilerplate; also closes the product page facts.
schema.press.naming: How to spell the product name in print.
schema.theme.accent: v2+. Per-app accent as a bare HSL triplet ("H S% L%"), contrast-gated at validation.
schema.marketing.sections: v2+. Ordered typed sections the product page renders through one renderer; kinds: features, steps, stats, showcase, table, faq, prose, terminal. Each may carry an optional "lift" beside its heading — the italic-serif half of the duet, one per heading, on the line carrying the promise. The page alternates its own grounds across this run; a kit chooses what to say, never where the bands fall.
schema.downloads: v3+. 1-4 real ways to get the product. The FIRST entry must be url-based — it renders as the hero primary button. Absent = the hero falls back to the repository link.
schema.downloads[].label: Button or chip text.
schema.downloads[].kind: appstore | releases | dmg | zip | exe | appimage | website | repo (url-based) or brew | script (command-based).
schema.downloads[].url: https:// URL, required for url-based kinds.
schema.downloads[].command: Copyable install command, required for brew/script.
schema.downloads[].note: Optional caveat shown near the CTA.
schema.assets: Every art file, flat basenames only, with role, label, note and MEASURED width/height (fetch re-measures and throws on mismatch).
schema.assets[].role: icon-card | icon-press | icon-vector | screenshot | screenshot-localized | lockup | hero | diagram | benchmark | terminal. icon-* / screenshot / lockup are singletons; screenshot-localized may repeat, once per language.
schema.assets[].file: Flat basename sitting next to this assets.json.
schema.assets[].label: Caption shown in the press kit.
schema.assets[].note: Format note on the download badge, e.g. "PNG".

product.name: VocalDrop
product.tagline: studio-grade acapella, on your own hardware
product.summary: Separates vocals from any track on your own CPU or GPU. Studio-grade results, and your audio never leaves the machine.

press.short: VocalDrop is a free AI vocal isolator and remover for macOS, Windows and Linux that runs entirely on your own hardware — no upload, no account, no watermark.
press.long: VocalDrop separates vocals from instrumentals at studio quality, running RoFormer models locally on your own machine — GPU-accelerated through Metal on Apple Silicon, multi-core CPU on Windows and Linux. Every run returns both stems, so it removes vocals as readily as it isolates them, and it converts formats, strips silence and handles video in the same pass. Your audio never leaves the computer; the first launch downloads the engine and models once, about 2 GB, and after that it works with no connection. Free, with no watermarks, no track limits and no subscription.
press.naming: Written "VocalDrop" — one word, capital V and D. Never "Vocal Drop" or "Vocaldrop".

items.title: Fast and Max models
items.body: The RoFormer model family UVR5 uses, offered at two qualities. Fast for a quick pass, Max when the mix is dense.

items.title: Both stems, one pass
items.body: The isolated vocal and the instrumental land together in the Results feed — separation is one job, not two runs.

items.title: Video too
items.body: Drop a music video or a movie clip; the audio is extracted, separated, and the stem you chose is re-muxed back in sync.

items.title: Fully scriptable
items.body: Everything the app does works from the CLI, with --json output for pipelines. Right-click Quick Actions on macOS into the bargain.

sections.heading: Two passes,
sections.intro: VocalDrop is built on the RoFormer separation models, run locally through audio-separator. Which one runs is the only choice the app asks you to make.

steps.title: Drop the file in
steps.body: Audio or video, one or a queue. Video is de-muxed, separated, and can be re-muxed back in sync with whichever stem you kept.

steps.title: Fast — a single pass
steps.body: One high-SDR BS-Roformer pass. Near real time on Apple Silicon, and enough for a clean source.

steps.title: Max — three models, blended
steps.body: Three RoFormer checkpoints run and their vocal estimates are weighted together, then de-reverbed and de-noised. Slower, and the one to reach for on a dense mix.

steps.title: Both stems land together
steps.body: The vocal and the instrumental come out of the same run, so a karaoke bed costs nothing extra.

sections.lift: the ones that upload your audio.
sections.heading: Against the usual suspects

sections.note: Every option the app exposes, with --json for pipelines.

sections.heading: Your audio never leaves the machine —
sections.body:
Most free vocal extractors are websites that upload your audio to someone else's server. VocalDrop runs the models locally on your own CPU or GPU, so the audio is never sent anywhere, and there is no track limit, watermark or subscription attached to the decision.

What does leave the machine, stated plainly: anonymous crash and usage diagnostics — never file contents, never paths, never personal data — the one-time engine and model download on first launch, a URL if you paste one in for the app to fetch, and the update check if you leave it on. That is the complete list.

items.a: The RoFormer family, the same architecture UVR5 ships, run through audio-separator — as a native desktop app, with no Python setup and no dependency roulette. Fast is a single pass; Max is a three-model ensemble, blended and cleaned up.
Yes. Free to use, with no watermarks, no track limits, no feature paywall and no account. It is closed source; the public repository holds the downloads and the README.
Only on the first launch, which downloads the engine and models once — about 2 GB for the full set, or roughly 200 MB if you only ever use Fast. After that separation is entirely offline.

They are processed on your machine and never uploaded. VocalDrop does send anonymous crash and usage diagnostics — never file contents, file paths or personal data — and the only other network calls are the one-time model download, a URL you paste in yourself, and the optional update check.

Apple Silicon Macs (M1 to M4), Windows 10 or 11 on x64, and Linux on x64. Intel-Mac builds are not provided. Separation is GPU-accelerated through Metal on Apple Silicon; Windows and Linux run on multi-core CPU, which is slower but just as offline.

items.q: Why does my Mac say it cannot open it?
items.a: The current builds are not code-signed or notarized yet, so Gatekeeper objects on first launch: right-click the app and choose Open. On Windows, SmartScreen wants More info, then Run anyway. Signed builds are on the roadmap.
Yes — a full CLI ships inside the app and mirrors everything the interface does, with --json output for pipelines. macOS also gets right-click Quick Actions in Finder.
